subject: Review cycle tactical runbook + approval queue
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft tactical runbook + approval queue (Q2 review cycle)

Team —

I put together a concise tactical runbook for the upcoming annual review window. Main objectives: keep the launch staggered across teams, limit visibility for sensitive L4+ changes, and centralize manager approvals in a single queue so exec exceptions are auditable.

Attachments: timeline_spreadsheet.xlsx (proposed phased dates), manager_ack_form_draft.docx (one-pager for managers), redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf

High-level asks:
- Legal sign-off on redaction & appeal language (Emma, can you take a quick pass?)
- Confirm we can use DocuSign for manager acknowledgements (Monica)
- Consultant input on calibration windows & headcount exceptions (Tara)

I'm proposing the following timeline (see sheet):
- 4/5–4/9: manager calibration & appeals prep (private)
- 4/12–4/16: manager acknowledgements (DocuSign, phased by org)
- 4/19–4/23: leadership approvals & compensation exceptions

Goal: quiet operational launch (no org-wide comms) until approvals close.

Connor
Senior Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft tactical runbook + approval queue (Q2 review cycle)

Connor —

Thanks for the clear draft. A couple of quick notes after scanning the attachments:

1) DocuSign: we can use the enterprise account but need an internal envelope template (Monica/IT to coordinate).
2) Manager ack form: please add a short field for "data handling confirmation" (managers confirm they removed PII from notes for public HR records).
3) Timeline: include a "quiet hold" date if legal requests changes so we don't flip any comms by accident.

I've looped in Emma (external counsel) for redaction language and Tara for calibration facilitation. Also tagging Priyom for the escalation matrix (if >2% of exceptions require CEO approval).

—Monica
People Ops

Date: 2027-04-01T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft tactical runbook + approval queue (Q2 review cycle)

Connor / Monica —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick read and a few recommended edits:

• Redaction wording: the attached redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf is a good start but please add explicit examples of what to remove from manager notes (salary ranges, personal health info, compensation plan IDs). That reduces downstream review time.
• Appeals: include a timeline in the appeal section (48–72 hours for initial HR triage).
• DocuSign: fine from a legal standpoint, but insist on the envelope retaining an audit log and manager IP if required.

If you want, I can mark up the PDF and return by EOD. Also advise adding a "quiet hold" clause as Monica suggested.

Emma
Acme Legal (external counsel)

Subject: Re: Draft tactical runbook + approval queue (Q2 review cycle)

Tara —

Quick question on facilitation: are you available the week of 4/5 to run two 90-minute calibration sessions (one for Engineering/Platform, one for Product/Sales)? We'd want external moderation to keep the exceptions conversation tight.

Also pushed an Approval Queue sheet (https://sheets.redwood.com/approval-queue-2027) — each manager row will capture: manager name, role band, proposed comp change, redaction status, HR triage outcome, leadership approver, and DocuSign envelope ID.

If we can keep the exception window to <=48 hours for leadership sign-off, operations can stay on schedule.

Connor

Subject: Re: Draft tactical runbook + approval queue (Q2 review cycle)

Connor / Monica —

Happy to run calibration sessions the week of 4/5. Availability: 4/6 afternoon (Eng/Platform) and 4/8 morning (Product/Sales). My recommendation: run a pre-read packet (10 minutes) + 90-minute moderated session, and follow up with a 30-minute exceptions triage.

On exceptions: we usually see 1–3% of roles needing leader-level adjustments; plan for up to 5% buffer for sensitive orgs. If you want, I'll prepare a one-slide "exception evaluation rubric" to speed leadership decisions.

Tara
Workforce Partners (external compensation & calibration consultancy)

Subject: Re: Draft tactical runbook + approval queue (Q2 review cycle) — leadership ask

Team —

Thanks for pulling this together, Connor. Two operational asks before we move to quiet launch:

1) Finalize the manager ack form with the data-handling confirmation field and a short note on appeals timing. Monica, can you produce v1 by EOD Monday?
2) Priyom, prepare an escalation brief (one pager) if exceptions exceed 2% or if more than one L4+ role is affected in the same org. We will reserve the right to pause comms if legal needs additional redactions.

Once those are in place, I'm comfortable with the phased approach. Please route any CEO-level exceptions to my inbox with the Approval Queue row ID and DocuSign envelope reference.

Vivek
VP, People & Ops
